recipes.name: Broiled Parmesan-Lemon Tilapia
ingredients_raw: 1 serving olive oil cooking spray (such as PAM®)
2 tablespoons butter-margarine blend (such as Smart Balance®), melted

steps.text: Preheat the oven's broiler and set the oven rack about 6 inches from the heat source. Line a broiler pan with aluminum foil. Spray the broiler pan's rack with olive oil cooking spray.
Sprinkle tilapia with sazon seasoning and arrange on the prepared broiler rack.
Cook the fillets under the preheated broiler until fish is barely opaque, 2 to 3 minutes per side.
Mix the Parmesan cheese, butter-margarine blend, fat-free mayonnaise, lemon juice, lemon zest, basil, black pepper, onion powder, and celery salt together in a bowl.
Spread the Parmesan cheese blend over the fish fillets, return to oven, and continue cooking until the topping is golden brown and the fish flakes easily, 3 to 5 more minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Broiled Parmesan-Lemon Tilapia

review.reviewBody:
Amazing tilapia recipe. All three of my kids loved this. I didn't have Sazon seasoning on hand so I used a mix of onion, garlic, paprika and parsley. Love the fact it is low carb!!!

So good that my husband wants to serve to company three days from now!!!!

My family loved it! My parents live with us and my daughter and her hubby and my husband and I were so surprised at how good it was! I did change things a bit, since Parmesan is so salty I did not add any salt. I also did not mix my Mayo and lemon juice and butter in the topping. I baked my tilapia with pepper only for 10 min, at 400 degrees under convection, it was frozen. I flipped it and then I spread the softened butter, then the Mayo and I poured the lemon juice in the pans. I mixed the parm, parsley, ground coriander and garlic powder with lemon zest. I patted that onto the Mayo, DUKES Mayo! (I am a southern cook) I used full fat butter because it is better for you than margarine. Then I put it back in the oven for 10 more min and then I turned on the broiler for about 5 min to crisp the top a bit. It was wonderful and juicy and flaky. My family even said it tasted like a restaurant made it! High compliments from my family! Thank you for the inspiration for this recipe!! I will make it over and over! This is good enough to serve to snooty company! Haha!

Didn't have sazon, so just used hungarian paprika,salt, pepper. Used fresh basil and real mayo, real butter.
I prepare fish often and this is the best tasting ever. Only broiled a minute on one side, 2 minutes after adding the parmesan mixture. I like my fish flaky.

I am eating this now and am definitely enjoying it. It was very simple to make. I didn't have everything the recipe requested, but I don't think that affected the taste any. I didn't have any lemon zest, so just omitted that. I didn't have any fat free mayo, so used regular. I didn't, as many reviewers have stated, have the Sazon seasoning, so I used the recipe so nicely shared by another reviewer: 1 tsp each of: salt, garlic powder, black pepper, paprika, cumin, coriander - this was more than enough for the four fillets.

One reviewer said she makes a double batch of the Parmesan topping to save as dipping sauce. I kept back a little of the liquid to try that and find it adds a really nice flavor to the finished fish.

The children haven't finished eating yet, but they haven't turned their noses up. Lol. I definitely will be making it again for myself.
Didn't have sazon seasoning so I just used equal parts paprika, cumin, coriander, and garlic salt. I also substituted 0% Fage yogurt for the mayo but used real butter.

This has become a favorite. I've served it for company several times over a bed of small leaf spinach and it continually gets rave reviews. It works fine to make the lemon-cheese paste up a day ahead and store in the frig. until ready to broil the fish. I cover a jelly roll pan with foil and broil the seasoned fish for 2 minutes and turn. Apply the lemon-cheese paste to the second side and slip under the broiler for another 2-3 minutes. Quick and delicious!

The recipe for sazon seasoning looks a lot like that for Madras Curry, which I had here so I used that. Also, based on complaints of the fish being too rich the first time I made it, I reduced the butter and mayonnaise by nearly half the second time around. Much better reviews in my crowd as a result and the cheese browned more too. This recipe is fast and easy and looks great on a plate.
Everyone loved this. I made my own sazon seasoning, substituting turmeric for the annatto, but otherwise I kept everything the same. My picky son said it was the best fish I'd ever made!

I have to post because this dish is delicious!! I hate fish but am on a low carb diet and heard Tilapia is one of the least fishy tasting fish so I was looking for a stellar recipe....this is it!! Thanks to another reviewer who posted this: I too had difficulty finding Sazon in my grocery stores - so I made my own after searching on google, 1 tsp each of: salt, garlic powder, black pepper, paprika, cumin, corriander

I followed the recipe and made the seasoning above. AMAZING!!

Based on all the 5 star ratings, I made this last night for company without testing it first and everyone loved it!! Delish. Based on another's suggestion, I made the sazon spice: 1 tsp each of: salt, garlic powder, black pepper, paprika, cumin, corriander (I crushed the seeds). Definitely a keeper!
Wonderful. I've made this many times. Now I halve the butter and use fat-free plain yogurt instead of mayo. I've used all different kinds of white fish. Really good.
Was kinda plain but went good with rice and veggies
My husband loved this recipe! It's easy to prepare and is ready in minutes.
Cut the sazon seasoning by half but add 2 teaspoons of lemon pepper. WOW will definitely be making again!!
Similar to another recipe from this site, but the Sazon was different, and yummy! Will make again!
Tasty, and ideal for when you don't have a lot of time (or don't feel like spending a lot of time to make dinner).
Superb
Made this identical recipe with salmon filets...Best salmon we ever ate!
Very easy to do! Tilapia was tasty and well cooked.
I didn't add the Miami seasoning, as I couldn't find that, but tasted awesome without it.
